bodyType.note: ONE shared mesh: body_type is a morph (+ joint offsets in race_rig.json) like the race sliders, continuous 0..1. The female atlas only differs by the painted band; gender picks the M_Body source texture + skin mask (texture swap), body_type the shape. Garments are gender-agnostic: every garment mesh carries the same-named body_type morph (drape variant) - drive it with the same weight as the body.

base.faceFeaturesNote: v3.1: separate feature nodes skinned 100% to Head; suppressFace names hide ALL nodes listed (nose = drawn Body_nose + every Body_nosem_<variant>, whichever is active). eyes+brows use M_Eye, mouth M_Mouth, drawn nose M_Nose (alphaMode MASK); mesh noses use M_Body skin texels
base.space: glTF Y-up, +Z forward; nodes named as in the GLB
base.style: clean flat colour bands (3-5 per region), hue-shifted ramps, no dither, no pure black/white

scalpSegments.note: hair_study: cranium of Body_head split into hideable nodes (same M_Body material/UVs, custom normals = full-head smooth normals, so shown pieces are seam-free). Hair styles list the ones they cover in hidesSegments and ship an inset hair-coloured cap part (<id>_scalp); headwear rules hide the crown. Body_head_liner (always shown, never hide it) is a skin copy of the whole scalp region 4-10 mm inside the head with the exact boundary verts, so any hidden combination stays closed. Hair shells were pushed out to clear every still-shown skin sample by 1.5 mm (HAIR_CLEAR) and hat-flattened hair is tucked 3 mm inside headwear over hidden scalp (HAT_TUCK).

belt.note: clothing_ff3: belts / sashes sit over every torso layer at the waist (3 fit morphs)

face_upper.label: Upper face
face_upper.holds: glasses, goggles, eyepatch, circlets, visor-free face items (over the eyes; drawn over a lower-face mask)

face_lower.label: Lower face
face_lower.holds: bandana (wear=mask), cloth masks, scarves pulled up (hide the mouth/nose, hide facial hair)

hairSlots.status: hair_parts v1: hair PARTS KIT (7 kit slots, 20 parts) + 27 painted scalp layers + 21 starter style recipes (hairStyles); 6 facial_hair assets; stubble texture layer, brow tint.

hair_cap.mesh: scalp cap: 8 big locks, K rows, lip ring, inset scalp cap part (<id>_scalp) over the segments it hides

hair_fringe.mesh: fringe plate hanging from under the cap front rim, stands forward of the forehead

hair_sides.mesh: side panels (L+R parts) in front of the ears

hair_back.mesh: back panel: wraps the back of the skull, then a slab behind the shoulders

hair_tail.mesh: ponytail / braid / bun / topknot (+ fixed-colour tie parts)

hair_spikes.mesh: spike clusters (pyramids, flat colour per facet) and the mohawk crest

hair_acc.mesh: hair accessories (headband; fixed cloth colour, not dyed)

facial_hair.mesh: mesh beard / moustache (skinned to Head; follows jaw_width, head_size, face params, body_type)

assetSchema.name: str
assetSchema.slot: hair_cap | hair_fringe | hair_sides | hair_back | hair_tail | hair_spikes | hair_acc | facial_hair
assetSchema.states: {full:{showParts:[..], morphs:{..}}, under_hat:{showParts|morphs (e.g. st_hair_flat:1)}, hidden:{}} - a missing state falls back via stateFallback
assetSchema.hidesSegments: [segment nodes] while the asset is visible (e.g. Body_ears_pointed for long hair over the ears) - same semantics as garments
assetSchema.dye: same encoding as garments (hair colour = one region)
assetSchema.raceFit: same weight/morph transfer as garments (all race sliders + body_type + face params on Head-weighted verts)

targets: M_Body / M_Body_f head texels (shared UV layout)
stubble.encoding: R = hair-ramp band*50, G = growth level*60 (1 chin+lip core .. 4 sideburns); a texel is painted when level <= ceil(stubble*4)
stubble.blend: texel = round(mix(skin texel, hairRamp[band], 0.62)) - flat, no dither; drawn over the skin swap AND over the scalp paint

hairColor.note: ONE colour per character drives every hair part (dye region "hair"), painted scalp layers, stubble and (browTint) the brows; rampFrom(rgb) like garment dyes (no pure black/white). Ties / headband are fixed colours (not dyed).

scalpPaint.control: scalpPaint (list of layer ids, drawn in order)
targets: M_ScalpPaint on the Body_scalp_paint* overlay nodes (own 512x512 tile UV)

hv3_part_L.name: v3 full hair, side part (character's left)

hv3_part_R.name: v3 full hair, side part (character's right)

hv3_pony_low.name: v3 pulled back to a low tie

hv3_pony_high.name: v3 pulled back to a high tie

hv3_bun_high.name: v3 pulled up into a crown bun

hv3_bun_low.name: v3 pulled back into a low bun

hv3_braid.name: v3 pulled back to a nape braid

hv3_braids2.name: v3 centre part to twin braids

fb_faux.name: Faux hawk (shaved sides + painted top strip)

scalpPaint.encoding: tile mask R = hair-ramp band*50 (0 = transparent), G = mode*60: 1 replace with hairRamp[band], 2 mix(skin texel, hairRamp[band], 0.62), 3 mix(skin texel, hairRamp[band], 0.16) = shaved stubble (hair_v2.1; 0.28 -> 0.16 in hair_v3.1: the shaved sides read as a helmet)
scalpPaint.uvmapEncoding: per tile pixel: R,G = body-atlas texel (x,y) under it, B=255 valid -> the skin texel used by mode 2

overlay.rule: overlay node visible iff scalpPaint is non-empty AND its segment (value; null = Body_head, never hidden) is not hidden. Texture = RGBA composite of the layers (alpha 255 where any layer paints, else 0; glTF alphaMode MASK).

scalpPaint.order: skin swap -> stubble overlay (body atlas); scalpPaint layers (in list order) -> overlay tile
scalpPaint.note: clothing_ff3 STEP 0: own 256x256 azimuthal tile on a 0.5 mm lifted overlay (~2.9x the body atlas density) instead of the ~25x9 cranium texels of the body atlas: clean pixel hairlines. Flat bands, no dither.

browTint.target: M_Eye atlas (brow pixels: palette B -> band 4, b -> band 3 of the hair ramp)

styles.note: hairStyles = recipes: paint (scalpPaint layer ids) + parts {kit slot: asset id}. Selecting a style clears every kit slot, then sets its parts and scalpPaint; the advanced mode edits slots / paint directly (style becomes "custom"). hidesSegments / tris are informative (union / sum of the parts, tris without the inset scalp caps). flavour = special looks kept from v1 (mohawk, topknot) on shaved/stubble sides.

randomize.note: gender-aware: a hairStyles recipe is drawn by weights[gender] (dwarf women favour braids); women only get facial hair as dwarves (small chance); the hair lock keeps style, slots, paint, stubble, colour, brow tint

hairLength.note: drop below each part root scaled (long, short); weight = max(0,v) on hl_len_long, max(0,-v) on hl_len_short. Buns / topknot / ties have no morph

beardLength.targets: facial_hair (hang below the jaw; moustache parts fixed)

hairGrey.targets: hair parts, scalp paint, brow tint

spec.rule: hair_v2.1 (flat bands, no per-texel dither): ramp = rampFrom(hairColor) (5 bands, band 1 lightest); for each band b in HSV: hue unchanged, s2 = s*(1-(1-satKeep)*grey), v2 = v+(bandV[b]-v)*grey. grey 0 = unchanged, grey 1 = silver ramp whose lightest band is near-white (v .95); the texture keeps its painted band index per texel, only the ramp colours move
spec.unity: toon hair shader: after the band lookup, lerp the band colour with float _Grey exactly as above (or bake the 5 shifted band colours on the CPU into the _Ramp texture / MaterialPropertyBlock when _Grey changes); beard material instance has its own _Grey

sliders.note: hair_v2: blendshape weights (Unity: SkinnedMeshRenderer.SetBlendShapeWeight(index of name, w*100)); the hl_ morphs are cleared against the skull like the base mesh and combine with sth_* state morphs. Randomize: grey is age-weighted (elder build/preset .55-1, others 8% .1-.4); lengths ~35% each ±.8

zones.note: headwear zones: hair_cap shells are split into zone parts <part>__<zone> (crown/sides/back/bangs/long; same UVs/weights/morphs, flat shading -> no visible seam); tail-slot assets = zone tails, crests = crown, headband = acc, scalp caps = scalp (never zone-hidden). Headwear hides / tucks zones via hairZones (see manifest.hairZones).
zones.classify: face centroid c (rest): long if c.z<longLine; crown if c.z>crownLine; bangs if |az|<=60 and c.z>=eye-.025, or a bang-morph vertex and |az|<=80; back if |az|>=115; else sides

layerBands_m.rule: a garment is built at band_of(layer) from the body; at overlap zones it is PROJECTED outward (layer_fit) until its shell, including the flat chords between ring vertices, clears the union of every inner layer it can be worn over (all their states, compressed regions compressed) by the gap; covered inner regions compress (st_cmp_*) instead of the outer layer inflating.

layerOffsets_m.note: shell distance from the body surface; outer layers must stay outside inner ones where they overlap

evaluation: 0. forceStates: rules whose `if` matches the selected states override those states (e.g. riding boots -> pants tucked)
visibleParts = alwaysParts + showParts of each selected state option
hiddenSegments = union(garment.hidesSegments, option.hidesSegments, rule.then.hideSegments) over equipped garments
rule `if` keys: garment id (with required states) or "@<slot>" = any equipped garment in that slot (condition {}); hideParts keys likewise, part list ["*"] = all parts
morph weights from option.morphs and rule.then.morphs (keys are globally unique, apply to every mesh that has the key); suppressFace hides those feature nodes (base.faceFeatures[name])
slots = option.slot || garment.slot, plus garment.occupiesSlots and rule occupiesSlots; two items on one slot = conflict (viewer auto-unequips the older one)
race sliders: set the same-named morph weights on garment meshes as on the body; joint offsets are on the shared skeleton
body_type (0 male .. 1 female) is one more race slider: set the same weight on the body AND every worn garment mesh; gender also swaps the M_Body source texture/skin mask (base.bodyType.genders)
rule `if` keys starting with "%" = any equipped garment or selected state option that carries that tag (garment.tags / option.tags)

compress (compressUnder): rule.then.compress = {target (garment id | @slot | %tag): [region names]}; for every equipped target garment that defines garment.compressRegions[region], set morph compressRegions[region].morph = 1 (unknown regions are ignored, so rules can name regions future garments will have)

layer order at overlap zones: effective layer = option.layer || garment.layer (shirt tucked 18 < pants 20 < shirt untucked 22); option.overSlots = this item sits over items of those slots where they overlap (loose pants hem over boots). Geometry is built so these orders hold (layerFit)

hair: for each hair slot with an asset, state = most restrictive of [default] + rule then.hairStates (order hairSlots.stateOrder); a state the asset lacks falls back (stateFallback); hidden -> no parts; visible asset parts = state.showParts, its hidesSegments join hiddenSegments; an EMPTY slot (no asset) is skipped
race_fit: weights: nearest-body-surface barycentric transfer (per-part source segments; pauldrons from torso+upper arm+neck = clavicle/upper-arm blend); race morphs: same slider fields evaluated at the garment vertices; state morphs are added on top.

zones.crown: top of the head above the hat-band line
zones.bangs: front locks / fringe over the forehead (bang morph region)
zones.long: everything hanging below the chin line (long hems, front locks below the jaw)
zones.scalp: inset scalp cap (never hidden by zones)

values.flat: zone visible; the asset is in its under_hat state (flattened by the hat_flattens_hair / headwear_flattens_hair rules)
values.tuck: zone visible + the headwear fit morph (fit) pulls it inside the shell / under the rim
values.hide: zone parts not shown (the scalp cap stays)

hairZones.evaluation: for every worn garment: merge garment.hairZones and the selected options' hairZones, most restrictive value per zone wins (order). A hair part with zone Z is shown only if its asset state shows it and zones[Z] != hide; fit morphs of every worn piece (hzfit_<gid>) are set to 1 (they exist on the hair zone meshes only: deltas that move flattened hair radially inside that piece's inner surface, 2.5 mm margin, never into the skin). Zones the rule does not name are show. hairLength / bangLength still clamp to <= 0 while any headwear is on (user values restored after).

outfitPresets.note: clothing_ff3: FF3-inspired looks built from ORIGINAL pieces. outfit = {garment: {state: option}}; dye = {garment: {region: [r,g,b]}} (missing = garment default).

hairPresets._note: applied by the viewer on preset select: style (hairStyles id -> kit slots + scalpPaint), facial_hair, stubble, hairColor, hairGrey/beardGrey/hairLength/bangLength/beardLength (hair_v2); missing keys = empty / 0

face.rule: recipes store garments by id + states, so outfits need no change: glasses -> face_upper, bandana wear=mask -> face_lower. A legacy 'face' slot LOCK maps to the face slot(s) its occupant uses (glasses -> upper, bandana mask -> lower), or to both when the slot was empty.
face.bandanaHeadState: bandana wear=head stays a head_inner item (tag headwear): a hat (head_outer) may sit over it, the headwear_flattens_hair rule puts every hair part in its under_hat state; it never touches the face slots. wear=neck is the neck slot.

randomize.rule: v4.1: pick from racePool (stylised sets only when raceGate allows them, max 15% chance); reject any ramp with allowed[skin] false -> never a hair hue close to a coloured skin. Defaults/presets never use stylised ramps.

hueCheck.compare: ramp base stop (pos .55) vs palette.SKIN_BASES[skin], HSV

hairColor.lut: 5 stops [pos 0..1, rgb]: deep .0, shade .30, base .55, light .80, highlight 1.0; colour = linear interpolation of the stops at value v (256-entry LUT texture per ramp; no banding, no dither)
hairColor.legacyRgb: old presets store hairColor rgb: pick the ramp whose base stop (pos .55) is nearest in RGB

hairGrey.rule: per LUT stop: rgb = mix(stop.rgb, silver[stop].rgb, grey); silver ramp below

hairLit.rule: Trailbound pixel lighting (4 bands, Bayer edge dither): band = lightBand(N.L) in [0..1] (the lighting pass output for this texel); final = albedo * mix(1, band, hairLit). hairLit 0 = fully unlit (painted value carries all the shading), 1 = full scene lighting. Hair defaults .35 because the crown highlight / tip darkening are already painted in.
hairLit.unity: Material float _HairLit; in the toon fragment: col.rgb = albedo * lerp(1, bandLight, _HairLit); keep _HairLit per material instance (beard has its own)
hairLit.viewer: paperdoll_test.html: uniform hairLit on the hair material; when the pixel-lighting pass is off, bandLight = 1 (flat albedo)

hairLength.targets: shells (hem below the hairline scaled about z .95/.995), tails (v3 rule)

bangLength.targets: front locks of every shell (|azimuth| < 50-72 deg)

valueMap.encoding: <id>_val.png: R = value 0..255 (crown highlight ~250 .. tips / underside ~40), G = 255 dyed hair, 0 = fixed colour (ties, headband: keep <id>.png)
valueMap.rule: albedo = G>127 ? LUT(ramp, grey)[R] : base texel; nearest filtering (texel art) but the value itself is a smooth gradient
